title: The Three Billy Goats Gruff
author: Traditional; adapted for Shellfie
credit: A gentle original adaptation of a traditional Norwegian folktale. Source: Popular Tales from the Norse, translated by George Webbe Dasent (1859), Project Gutenberg #8933.

pages: Three goats saw green grass on a hill.
A bridge led to the hill. A troll lived below it.
The little goat went first. Trip, trap!
“Who is on my bridge?” asked the troll.
“It is me,” said the goat. “May I cross?”
“Yes,” said the troll. The little goat crossed.
The middle goat came next. Trip, trap!
“May I cross too?” the goat asked.
“Yes,” said the troll. The middle goat crossed.
The big goat came last. TRIP, TRAP!
“Your bridge is strong,” said the big goat.
“Thank you,” said the troll. “I fixed it today.”
The goats ate grass. The troll rested by the bridge.

quiz.q: Where did the goats want to go?
quiz.ev: Three goats saw green grass on a hill.

quiz.q: Why did the goats use the bridge?
o: They wanted to find a boat
